title: Genome mining and deep learning prioritize antimicrobial peptides from Bacillus genomes
summary: Mining 3,283 Bacillus genomes yielded 6,532 putative antimicrobial peptides in 682 cluster families. APEX-based MIC predictions prioritized 73 candidates, four of which were synthesized; they showed species-dependent antibacterial activity, strongest against Clostridium perfringens. Prediction and experiment correlated at r = 0.967-0.970 for three species but negatively for A. baumannii (r = -0.557) and Salmonella Typhimurium (r = -0.619).
ai_technology: APEX deep-learning model predicting minimum inhibitory concentrations, used to prioritize mined peptides

evidence.tested: Four peptides chosen from 73 predicted high-potency candidates were chemically synthesized and tested for antibacterial activity.
evidence.unknown: Only four peptides were tested; prediction-experiment agreement was negative for two species; clinical potential is not assessed. Abstract-based; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: APEX MIC predictions ranked 6,532 mined peptide sequences down to 73 candidates for synthesis.
